sense: of a speech, a joke: be received coldly

terms.gloss: fall flat, be coldly received, flag
terms.grammar: verb, second conjugation, intransitive; no perfect in use
evidence: Ter. Eun. 3.3.11: sermōnem quaerere; ubi friget, hūc ēvāsit (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The verb is “to be cold”; of a speech, a joke or a conversation, to be flat or dull, and of a person, to be coldly received.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 98, checked against the searchable text and the page image (12 November 2026).
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
